items.why_watch: Jessica Kellgren-Fozard digs into the structural and social reasons why women — particularly queer women and women of color — face harsher public backlash than their male counterparts for comparable behavior. At 44 minutes, it's a proper essay-style video that goes beyond surface-level takes, drawing on specific examples rather than vibes. If you've ever noticed the pattern but couldn't fully articulate why it happens, this gives you the vocabulary.

items.title: Who Was the God Jove?
items.description: Jove, also known as Jupiter, was the supreme god in Roman Mythology. The two share the same features and characteristics. In Roman mythology, Jove was the son of Saturn and the husband of Juno, the queen of the gods. He was the equivalent of the Greek god Zeus and was considered the most powerful of all the gods. After he took credit for rescuing his brothers and sisters from their father Cronus, Zeus became king of heaven and gave his brothers, Poseidon and Hades, the sea and the underworld, re
items.why_watch: A compact seven-minute primer on Jove/Jupiter that clearly untangles his relationship to Zeus and explains why the Romans gave him a distinct identity despite borrowing heavily from Greek mythology. It's the kind of foundational reference video that fills in gaps you didn't know you had — useful if you keep encountering Jupiter in literature, art, or astrology without a firm grasp of who he actually was. Short enough to watch between tasks.

discovery_articles.title: Branch Davidian Compound in Axtell, Texas
discovery_articles.snippet: Near Axtell, Texas, 20 miles north-east of Waco was a large group of buildings known as the Mount Carmel Center once used by the Branch Davidian religious group. Named after the Biblical mountain Mount Carmel in Israel, the Davidians (later Branch Davidians) lived in relatively peaceful isolation from the Waco community. As a city with deep religious roots itself, Waco generally accepted the Branch Davidians and allowed them to practice their religious beliefs without interference.

discovery_articles.title: Doña Manolita in Madrid, Spain
discovery_articles.snippet: Few phenomena can reliably unite the notoriously fragmented population of Spain, but the obsession with El Gordo —the nation’s historic Christmas lottery—is unquestionably one of them. At the heart of this annual ritual of collective hope stands a single legendary shop in the capital, whose origins trace back to a remarkably ambitious young woman. In 1904, a 25-year-old woman named Manuela de Pablo opened a modest lottery stand on Madrid’s Calle San Bernardo.

discovery_articles.title: Stillman’s Run Battle Site Memorial in Stillman Valley, Illinois
discovery_articles.snippet: In 1832, counties in central Illinois were calling for volunteers to protect the frontier from Black Hawk and his Sauk warriors. On the morning of May 14, 1832, tensions came to a head. Black Hawk’s warriors discovered Major Isaiah Stillman and nearly 300 militia men had set up camp uncomfortably close by, near Sycamore Creek in what is now Ogle County.

news.title: My High-Protein Hack for Making the Creamiest Scrambled Eggs
news.snippet: Cottage cheese really is that girl right now. Hailey Bieber’s eating it with her signature meatballs, I’m eating it on toast with roasted tomatoes, and people on TikTok are seemingly throwing it into just about every recipe for some extra proteinoc. One dish I have been surprised to see people add cottage cheese to is scrambled eggs.
news.blurb: Cottage cheese is quietly staging a very delicious takeover, and this scrambled egg hack might just be the reason you finally keep a tub in the fridge.

news.title: How to turn excess green vegetables into a vibrant Spanish soup – recipe | Waste not
news.snippet: A gazpacho is not only a great way to use up odds and ends in the crisper drawer, it will also surprise you with its flavour and versatility Since reading How Not to Die , by Michael Greger, I’m always looking for ways to include greens in every meal. He regularly pops into my mind when I’m cooking, whispering in my ear: “Add some spinach to that risotto,” say, or “Moringa powder will make your porridge much more nutritious.” So I’m sure today’s green gazpacho would make him proud. It’s a great way to clear out your crisper drawer and pack a meal with all sorts of greens.
news.blurb: A green gazpacho that rescues the forgotten depths of your crisper drawer while delivering genuine flavour? Consider this your most virtuous summer read.
